Context:
**Project overview of Auto Task via Google Meeting (Salesforce DX), with risks found**

This was a read-only review of the whole project. No code was changed. The app connects each user to Google, and a scheduled job then works through each active Meeting_Configuration__c in turn. For each one it pulls the Gemini meeting notes from Google Drive (Google Docs whose names start with '<Config Name> -'), reads the 'Suggested next steps' section and creates Meeting_Task__c records with status 'Pending Reviewed'. When a task is approved, a record-triggered flow creates a standard Task. The review found a deployment blocker and a silent-failure bug, listed under open issues.

**Open issues**
- MeetingTaskBatch calls MeetingTaskHelper.getAssigneeIdByNameMatch, but no MeetingTaskHelper class exists in force-app. Deploying from this repo will fail unless the class already exists in the target org. Get it from the org or write it.
- If GoogleAuth.getValidAccessToken() returns a blank token, MeetingNotesQueueable.execute returns without calling moveToNext(). The job chain stops, so every configuration after the failing one is skipped for that run. That return also comes before `insert logs`, so the 'Authentication token is blank.' Meeting_Log__c is never saved and the failure leaves no record.
- Tokens come from the running user's User record (GoogleAuth.getValidAccessToken). The scheduled job therefore uses the Google account of whoever scheduled it, not the account of each configuration's owner.
- objects/User/ has about 90 field files from managed packages (Pardot, Maps, SBQQ, et4ae5 and others). Only the four Google_* fields belong to this project. Deploying the whole folder may conflict with those packages, so consider trimming it.
- There are no Apex test classes or LWC Jest tests in the repo, so the code can't reach the test coverage Salesforce requires to deploy to production.
- Video_Meeting__c appears to be an older data model that the main notes-to-tasks process doesn't use. It is a candidate for removal once that is confirmed.
- The project folder is not a git repository yet.

**Touched:** force-app/main/default/classes/MeetingTaskBatch.cls, force-app/main/default/classes/MeetingNotesQueueable.cls, force-app/main/default/classes/MeetingNotesScheduler.cls, force-app/main/default/classes/GoogleAuth.cls, force-app/main/default/flows/Meeting_Task_After_Save_Flow.flow-meta.xml, force-app/main/default/objects/User/fields

**Options for upgrading the project: API version, tooling and Google auth design**

The user asked how to upgrade the project. Claude answered with recommendations only and changed no code. The user has not yet said which kind of upgrade they mean, and nothing has been decided. The suggested order was: run git init, align the API version, retrieve or write MeetingTaskHelper, add Apex tests with HttpCalloutMock, then move Google OAuth to Named Credentials.

**Open issues**
- API version mismatch: sfdx-project.json has sourceApiVersion 65.0, but all 11 versioned metadata files are on 66.0. Align them, using the org's maximum version from `sf org display` if you want the latest.
- OAuth is built by hand. GoogleAuth hardcodes the Google auth and token URLs, GoogleCalendarService.cls also calls the token endpoint itself, endpoints are allowed through Remote Site Settings, and access and refresh tokens are stored in custom Google_* fields on User, where they may be readable. Proposed fix (not agreed yet): an External Credential with per-user principals plus a Named Credential, called as `callout:...`. This would also remove most of GoogleAuth and the GoogleOAuthCallback Visualforce page, and it is the natural place to fix the scheduled-job running-user problem.
- Since the folder is not a git repo, the husky and lint-staged pre-commit hooks in package.json never run.
- Upgrading the npm dev dependencies (ESLint 9 and the LWC plugins) may need changes to eslint.config.js.

**Enterprise-readiness assessment of Auto Task via Google Meeting, which found a token leak to the browser**

The user asked whether the project is ready for enterprise use. The verdict was no: it is a single-org proof of concept. Rechecking the code found a new critical security issue: every connected user's Google access token is sent to the browser. It also confirmed that tokens and the OAuth client secret are stored in plain text. No code was changed. Claude offered to fix the token leak, and the user has not replied yet.

**Open issues**
- CRITICAL: the user-filter method in GoogleGeminiService (about line 105) runs SELECT Id, Name, Google_Access_Token__c FROM User and returns those User records through an @AuraEnabled UserFilterWrapper.users. Any user who can open the LWC can read every connected colleague's live Google token in browser dev tools, and that token can read their Drive. Fix: remove the token from the query (use the token only for a server-side filter, or a separate IsNotBlank check) or return a DTO with only Id and Name. Fix this before any further rollout.
- The Google_Access_Token__c and Google_Refresh_Token__c fields on User are unencrypted LongTextArea fields. Meeting_PS gives read and edit access to both, and Video_Meeting_PS also grants permissions on them, so admins and permission-set holders can see the tokens.
- The Google_Token__mdt object, which holds Client_Secret__c (a plain Text field), has Public visibility, so the OAuth client secret is not protected. This adds to the case for the proposed (not yet agreed) move to an External Credential with per-user principals plus a Named Credential.
- Other enterprise gaps: an AppExchange security review is needed if the app will be sold; the Drive-wide OAuth scope usually needs approval from the customer's Google Workspace admin; and token revocation, callout limits and scaling to many configurations are not handled.

**Object inventory for Auto Task via Google Meeting: what to deploy and what's legacy**

The user asked how many objects the app needs. The answer was 5: four custom objects (Meeting_Configuration__c, Meeting_Note__c, Meeting_Task__c, Meeting_Log__c) and the Google_Token__mdt custom metadata type, plus the 4 Google_* fields on User. All are already defined in force-app/main/default/objects and get created by deploying the folder. Nothing in the project was changed.

**Open issues**
- Video_Meeting__c is confirmed unused by Apex. Only the Auto_Task_via_Google_Meeting app and the Video_Meeting_PS permission set refer to it. If you remove the object, remove those references too or the deploy will fail.
- Google_Token__mdt (Google OAuth config, read by GoogleAuth and GoogleCalendarService) is easy to miss: it is a custom metadata type, not a custom object, and it needs its records filled in after deploy.
- objects/User/fields has 113 files. Only the 4 Google_* fields belong to this project, so deploy just those.
